bull.b: FDA approval converts Scholar Rock from a development-stage biotechnology company into a commercial neuromuscular business. ISEMBYLD’s first-in-class muscle-targeted positioning and clinically meaningful motor-function results provide a differentiated foundation for adoption and future expansion.

Rapid engagement with leading SMA treatment centers demonstrates effective launch execution and broad access to specialist prescribers. Early enrollment across major and additional centers can support durable patient acquisition as reimbursement processes mature and treatment pathways become established.

Regulatory progress in Europe and Japan expands the potential geographic reach of apitegromab, while FSHD and other anti-myostatin programs broaden the pipeline. These efforts create multiple future growth avenues beyond the initial U.S. SMA launch.

bear.b: The company remains far from sustained profitability, with very large losses relative to minimal product revenue. Until commercial sales scale substantially, ongoing research, development, and launch expenses will continue to weigh on earnings and limit internally funded growth.

bear.t: Heavy Cash Burn And Funding Needs
bear.b: Persistent negative operating and free cash flow means the business does not currently fund its obligations through operations. Continued investment in commercialization and development therefore depends on available financing, increasing sensitivity to execution and capital-access conditions.

Reimbursement delays can defer prescriptions converting into treated patients and revenue, even when underlying demand is strong. Prior authorization, appeals, and formulary processes may therefore slow the ramp of ISEMBYLD and make near-term commercial execution uneven.
